question.text: A bull spread in commodity futures is created when:

answer.text: The actual spread is more than the fundamental spread, with the expectation that it will narrow
The actual spread is less than fundamental, expecting widening
The trader expects prices to rise sharply
Both legs are bought at the same time

explanation.text: The Logic: A bull spread is created when the actual spread is more than the fundamental spread and is expected to narrow. The trader buys the near-month and sells the far-month, profiting as the spread narrows. The Trap: A bear spread is when the actual spread is less than the fundamental spread and is expected to widen. A bull spread is not a directional view on prices, and it is not built by buying both legs simultaneously.
